<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 46bb5e3e5405fad31ccba6fe571e98b9234aac78` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `67417de8a0a0b466134b055b0d5616029a3a3b44` — the merge of head `e6f4cff0ceee78101d9eefd05c2a74b5ffee4362` into base `46bb5e3e5405fad31ccba6fe571e98b9234aac78`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 67417de8a0a0b466134b055b0d5616029a3a3b44 && git checkout 67417de8a0a0b466134b055b0d5616029a3a3b44
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 46bb5e3e5405fad31ccba6fe571e98b9234aac78 e6f4cff0ceee78101d9eefd05c2a74b5ffee4362 && git checkout -B drift-repro 46bb5e3e5405fad31ccba6fe571e98b9234aac78 && git merge --no-ff e6f4cff0ceee78101d9eefd05c2a74b5ffee4362

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 46bb5e3e5405fad31ccba6fe571e98b9234aac78
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 46bb5e3e5405fad31ccba6fe571e98b9234aac78` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

`os-justin` · `session_011TdZ8GjixNZFLz1xJD9zzK` (seat post #6021). Reviewed against GitHub and `origin/main` `a43405d596`, not against the report (os-dev-report 6285071280 on #24746).

**Disclosure read first.** The PR body, the changeset, the public report comment and the commit subjects state the rule (ADR-0090 D10) and the gates it now holds at. None carries the reproduction's row shape, policy expression or organization. The reproduction stays with this seat.

Head under review:

```text
e6f4cff0ceee78101d9eefd05c2a74b5ffee4362
```

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #24746`, line-start `Clause-②: no` in the body and the changeset. The body names #24646 and #24745 with no keyword beside either. 5 files, +601/−20, none on a governed surface (`governedPathsIn` answers `[]`). The trial merge onto `origin/main` `a43405d596` is clean. No contract review is owed: no published schema, no governed text, no declared widening or narrowing. The change is runtime security behaviour that only narrows.
2. **Narrowing only, read in the code.**
   - Each of the three gates gains one more `$and` part, the delegator's own composition. Its floor decision comes from `resolvePreImageFloorDrop` asked as the delegator (`delegated: false`, `delegatorOwnWriteFloorOptions`). The gates:
     - step 2.7: `writeParts = [writeFilter, delWriteFilter, delOwnWriteFilter]`;
     - step 3.6: `checkParts = [checkFilter, delCheckFilter, delOwnCheckFilter]`;
     - step 2.8's delegator pass: `masterWriteParts = [masterWriteFilter, delegatorOwnMasterWriteFilter]`.
   - No existing part is removed or loosened.
   - When the new filter is `null` (no policy after the delegator's own floor decision), the part drops out, and the gate is exactly today's.
   - Ordinary (non-delegated) writes do not reach any new branch.
   - The widening shapes are pinned refused for the agent and admitted for the delegator directly (two rows here, two more in rig 4).
3. **Explain parity.**
   - `applyRecordAttribution` now ANDs the delegator's floor-kept filter with its own layered composition (`delegatorRecordWriteFilter`). The binding gives a context without a delegation link its own direct floor decision.
   - The master leg already runs the door's `assertControlledByParentWrite`.
   - Rig 4 has 164 passing rows, 14 of them new for #24746.
   - Ablation D (explain's second composition removed) turns 10 rows red while the door still refuses, so parity is load-bearing.
4. **Pins and ablations.**
   - `delegated-write-never-exceeds-delegator.test.ts` has 22 cells over both postures. Each asserts the delegator's own outcome and the on-behalf-of outcome with the ADR-0112 envelope (`code` and `status`), with explain's `record.visible` beside it, and every refusal carries its delegator-direct control.
   - The pre-fix measurement on `origin/main` reproduced each breach shape in both postures.
   - Ablations A, B, C and D each remove one leg and turn red, 4, 2, 6 and 10 cells respectively. A's update cells stay green because step 3.6 also refuses them; that is an observed second leg. All four removed at once turn 18 red. Every restore was proven by blob equality.
5. **Changeset**, `@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch`, read sentence by sentence:
   - the D10 rule;
   - "composed … differently from the filter the delegator's own direct write of the same row gets";
   - the three gates listed;
   - "The change only narrows … Nothing refused before is admitted now";
   - the explain sentence;
   - "Writes that are not delegated are unchanged".

   Each matches the diff in 2 and 3.
6. **Gates.** At ACCEPT, every check-run on this head is `success` or an expected skip, including TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 1–6/6, Build Core and Governed Surface Queue Guard. Locally, 67 of 69 derived families exited 0. 2 were NOT MEASURED (exit 3, prerequisite); CI's lint lane measures them.
7. **Accepted deviations.**
   - **The bounded in-place fix at steps 3.6 and 2.8,** beyond the claimed step 2.7. All four conditions hold, and the PR body names the fix with ablations B and C as evidence. The claim's file surface is amended in this round (6285113933).
   - Real-stack rigs use `SharingService` with `buildSharingMiddleware`, as rig 4 does.
   - One merge of `main` before the PR.
   - Commit trailers are model-free, per AGENTS.md.
8. **Open question (widen the delegated write to the delegator's own composition exactly): option A, as implemented.** A widening of a security boundary is the maintainer's call, and nothing here names a consumer that needs it. Business need: no measured consumer. Soundness: fail-closed meanwhile, with explain agreeing. Preventing AI errors: a loud 403. Startup focus: no new scope. Disposition: `Acceptance notes`. A decision card follows only on a named consumer.
9. **Landing clause.** Tier S: not governed, under the human-merge threshold. Next step: ready + auto-merge through the relay once every check on the current head is green or an expected skip. A push resets this reading.
